programme: CEBPA, CEBPG, HNF1B, NR5A2, HNF4G, TRERF1 and TCF21 share the target signature of the hepatocyte/steroidogenic nuclear-receptor cistrome: cholesterol and bile-acid handling (LDLR, ABCG5, ABCG8, SCARB1, CETP, CYP7A1), steroid/glucocorticoid synthesis (CYP11A1, CYP17A1, STAR, HSD3B2, HSD11B1, NR5A1), and endoderm/hepatic identity genes (HNF4A, HNF1A, ONECUT1, AFP, TTR, SERPINA1). CEBPA and CEBPG extend the same node into secretory-epithelial identity (SCGB1A1, SFTPD) and neutrophilic innate-immune output (CSF3R, CSF3, S100A8, PRTN3, IL1B, IL6). FOXJ1 (motile ciliogenesis), FHL2 (NFkB/cell-cycle cofactor), ZNF217 (amplicon oncogene/EMT) and SOX7/AEBP1 (endothelial and macrophage lipid handling) do not belong to this axis and are not part of the account below.
role_in_a: In COPD, this node's canonical output includes SERPINA1 (alpha-1-antitrypsin, the field's clearest monogenic emphysema/COPD risk gene, an HNF1B target here) and HSD11B1-driven local glucocorticoid regeneration, which bears on steroid responsiveness in airway disease; CEBPA/CEBPG's branch sets club-cell secretory genes (SCGB1A1, SFTPD) and the CSF3R/S100A8/IL1B/IL6 neutrophilic programme that dominates COPD airway inflammation.
role_in_b: In glioma/GBM, malignant glial cells are largely cholesterol auxotrophic and depend on exogenous cholesterol uptake and steroid-pathway intermediates for membrane biogenesis rather than de novo synthesis; ectopic activity of this normally hepatic/steroidogenic module (HNF1B, NR5A2, HNF4G, TRERF1, TCF21) would represent ectopic lineage-inappropriate reactivation supporting that lipid demand, consistent with the retrieved HNF1B/EMT-angiogenesis and NR5A2/chemoresistance findings even though those papers describe non-metabolic mechanisms.
shared_axis: The proposed link is not tissue lineage (lung epithelium and glia do not share hepatic ancestry) but convergent metabolic stress: chronic inflammatory remodeling in COPD and malignant proliferation in glioma may each reactivate this cholesterol/steroid-handling transcriptional module outside its native hepatic/adrenal context to meet local lipid and corticosteroid-metabolism demand.
reasoning: The seven carrying factors do form a real, nameable module defined by shared canonical targets (cholesterol/bile-acid/steroid genes), and it is not on the tissue-generic exclusion list, so its recurrence in both a lung and a brain cohort is not simply tissue background. But no retrieved paper documents this metabolic mechanism operating in either disease specifically — the two glioma-side papers (HNF1B, NR5A2) describe EMT/angiogenesis and miRNA-chemoresistance mechanisms, not steroidogenesis, and no paper addresses both diseases together, so the cross-disease bridge rests on domain reasoning about GBM cholesterol dependency and COPD steroid biology rather than on anything in the record.
support: PMID 34475987 — HNF1B via lncRNA-PVT1 drives EMT/angiogenesis in glioma, placing HNF1B mechanistically in disease B (not via the metabolic axis). PMID 36303447 — miR-433-3p downregulation of NR5A2 alters cisplatin chemosensitivity in glioma, placing NR5A2 in disease B via a chemoresistance route. PMID 29506519 — RNAseq of bronchial epithelial cells implicates CEBPG among COPD-associated genes/SNPs, placing CEBPG in disease A. PMID 39063108 and PMID 18398044 — TCF21 tied to lung-aging apoptosis biology and to promoter methylation in a lung malignancy context, placing TCF21 in disease A. No PMID in the record addresses the cholesterol/steroidogenic mechanism itself in either disease, and none address both diseases together.
how_to_falsify: Profile HNF1B, NR5A2, HNF4G, TRERF1 and TCF21 binding (ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN) at CYP11A1, CYP17A1, CYP7A1, STAR, ABCG5/ABCG8 and SCARB1 in patient-derived GBM lines and in COPD bronchial epithelial samples; if occupancy is absent, or if cholesterol-loading/LXR-agonist perturbation in GBM cells and glucocorticoid-pathway readouts after HNF1B/NR5A2 knockdown in airway epithelium show no dependence on these factors, the module is not functionally operative in either tissue and the account fails.
caveats: Brain and lung share no developmental lineage, so any hepatocyte-type module found active in both is inherently a stretch unless independently validated per tissue. The 299 patient-group comparisons are drawn from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so apparent robustness across 'comparisons' does not multiply the number of independent observations. The single-view exclusion list (GLIS3, SMARCA4, CDX1, etc.) confirms this account is not built on one subgroup's idiosyncrasy, and the tissue-generic exclusion list (FOXP3, RFX5, STAT4, EGR4, HDAC7) shows a separate immune-generic set was already screened out — neither exclusion validates the steroidogenic story itself. Five of the twelve concordant factors (FOXJ1, FHL2, ZNF217, AEBP1, SOX7) sit outside this programme entirely, so the account covers roughly half the list, not all of it. Notably, the two highest-recurrence factors, TRERF1 (188/299) and CEBPA (179/299), have no disease-specific Open Targets association or judgeable literature support at all, so the strongest quantitative signal in the data is the weakest evidenced part of the story.
